# Module and Calculation-Candidate Inventory

## Purpose and Denominator

`manifests/module-inventory.json` is the deterministic TOOLS-D1 index for
every tracked implementation source file and governed configuration module in
the repository. It scans recognized Python, Python stub, JavaScript,
TypeScript, Rust, MATLAB, C/C++, Arduino, shell, PowerShell, HTML, CSS, Prisma,
JSON, YAML, TOML, INI, XML, URDF, and web-manifest files. Tests are evidence
inputs rather than implementation rows. Generated, vendored, archived,
experimental, example, documentation, resource, and manual trees are excluded
explicitly in the manifest, so a consumer can reproduce the exact denominator.
The index binds bounded entry shards by normalized SHA-256, contiguous index,
entry count, and first/last path. Both the index and every shard remain below
the repository's one-megabyte file budget; consumers reassemble one logical
view only after verifying every shard and the exact declared shard set.

At this baseline, 3,429 modules are classified: 808 conservative calculation
candidates and 2,621 non-calculation modules. One legacy JavaScript file has a
non-UTF-8 encoding and remains explicitly blocked rather than being decoded by
an implicit platform default. These counts describe inventory coverage only;
they are not test coverage, calculation approval, or publication readiness.

## Deterministic Identity and Integrity

Each file receives a provisional path-derived identifier and a SHA-256 digest
of normalized text bytes. The normalization maps CRLF and bare CR to LF before
hashing. For module path (p_i) and normalized content digest (h_i), the tree
authority is

\[
H_{\mathrm{tree}} = \operatorname{SHA256}\!\left(
  \big\Vert_{i=1}^{n} p_i \mathbin{:} h_i \mathbin{\texttt{\\n}}
\right),
\]

where rows are ordered by normalized repository-relative path. This contract
makes the result independent of Windows checkout line endings while retaining
content changes. The path-derived identifier is not a stable calculation ID;
TOOLS-D3 owns stable equation-to-code identities that survive file movement.

## Classification Contract

A module is a `calculation` candidate only when its normalized path contains a
governed calculation marker, such as dynamics, kinematics, pressure drop,
signal processing, geometry, solver, energy, force, or trajectory, or when the
source imports a recognized scientific mathematics library. All other modules
are `non-calculation`. This intentionally conservative static screen can have
false positives and false negatives, so every calculation candidate has
`authority_status=provisional` and `review_status=review-required`.

The inventory also records language, purpose where statically available,
maintainer family, public surfaces and routes, mapped tests and validation,
ADRs, equation references, literal units, citations, artifact digests, risk
tags, normalized byte count, and content digest. Missing tests, sources, units,
chapters, equation pathways, validation, routes, or artifact digests remain
`unavailable`, `not-applicable`, or explicitly pending their owning subepic;
they are never synthesized. Non-calculation status
means only that the conservative detector found no calculation signal. It does
not waive public-API, security, licensing, accessibility, or downstream
compatibility review.

## Consumer and Failure Contract

The repository-owned schema is
`schemas/module-inventory.schema.json`, version
`tools-module-inventory/1.0.0`. It extends the program-owned calculation
registry without copying or competing with that shared schema. Both JSON Schema
validation and the Python consumer reject unknown fields, unsupported versions,
unsafe paths, invalid hashes, duplicate identifiers, unsorted duplicate
traceability arrays, denominator mismatches, and unsupported state values.

Any tracked in-scope module addition, removal, rename, or normalized content
change makes `--check` fail until the manifest is regenerated and reviewed. A
green inventory check proves only deterministic classification and freshness of
this file-level baseline. Public projection remains blocked until the remaining
manual, renderer, semantic, page, accessibility, licensing, digest, and human
approval gates are complete.
